paper_metadata.title: Leveraging LLM for Automated Ontology Extraction and Knowledge Graph Generation
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper presents OntoKGen, an LLM-assisted interactive pipeline for extracting a user-tailored ontology from targeted RAM-domain knowledge, generating a knowledge graph from comprehensive engineering text under that confirmed ontology, and optionally producing Cypher MERGE queries for Neo4j. The system uses an adaptive iterative chain-of-thought procedure and human confirmation to reduce ontology ambiguity and support structured retrieval, analysis, and future RAG use.

problem_addressed: Automate extraction and organization of relevant, structured knowledge from long, complex Reliability and Maintainability technical documents, especially semiconductor-equipment material, because manual extraction and KG construction are labor-intensive, error-prone, and may yield incomplete or inconsistent representations. The objective is a user-tailored ontology and KG that supports querying, analysis, and decision-making.

methodology.primary_family: Zero-shot and few-shot LLM prompting (without task-specific model training)
methodology.description: OntoKGen is an interactive, human-in-the-loop LLM system using OpenAI's API and an adaptive iterative CoT algorithm. Execution order: (1) the user supplies a predefined ontology or targeted text; (2) the LLM proposes/refines concepts, then relationships, then node properties, each confirmed by the user; (3) the confirmed ontology becomes the schema blueprint; (4) comprehensive text is supplied; (5) creation iterates over ontology concepts to create nodes and properties, then over relationships to create edges, then fills properties; (6) review re-reads the text for missing aligned instances/relations and reviews the graph for incorrect, unconnected, or missing links; (7) on approval, the system generates Cypher MERGE commands to populate Neo4j. Conversation history is retained to maintain context and guide users back to the active stage.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The ontology is extracted and confirmed before KG generation and explicitly constrains it. It comprises concepts/node classes, relationships/edge types, and node attributes. In the case study it included Equipment System, Equipment States, Sub-States, Activities, and Metrics; Has State, Has Sub-State, Has Activity, and Has Metric; mandatory id and name plus a user-specified brief explanation. The system uses the ontology as a structural blueprint to avoid ambiguity and enforce a consistent graph.

The ontology serves as a blueprint, ensuring the KG is generated with a clear and consistent representation of domain-specific knowledge.

input_output.input_type: User-provided predefined ontology or targeted natural-language text for ontology extraction, followed by comprehensive unstructured engineering-domain text; the source document may contain text, tables, and graphs, but the case study primarily uses textual content.
input_output.input_granularity: A short user query, detailed targeted text, or part of the comprehensive document is used initially; then the complete source document is reviewed, described as lengthy and technically complex.
input_output.output_representation: A property knowledge graph of nodes, typed relationships, and node properties, visualized and stored in Neo4j; optional Cypher MERGE commands create the nodes and relationships. The case-study graph represents equipment-system states, sub-states, activities, and metrics.

models_and_tools: Large language model (specific model not reported)
datasets: Background Statement for Semiconductor Draft Document 6578 (case-study source document; RAM domain; semiconductor manufacturing equipment)

evaluation.setting: Single qualitative human-in-the-loop case study in the RAM domain, applied to semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The authors visually inspect the generated Neo4j KG and describe accuracy, completeness, efficiency, and user interaction; there is no reported quantitative evaluation, benchmark comparison, baseline, dataset split, or numerical metric. Competency-question-based accuracy evaluation is only proposed for future work.

value: The case study produced a Neo4j KG grounded in a confirmed ontology of equipment-system concepts, states, sub-states, activities, metrics, relationships, and properties.
The authors report qualitatively that every concept, sub-state, activity, and metric in the comprehensive text was represented in the graph.
The KG-generation phase required minimal user interaction after ontology confirmation, while the ontology phase incorporated user-specific requirements.
No quantitative accuracy, completeness, efficiency, or competency-question results are reported; therefore the paper provides no numerical performance results or comparative claims.

evidence.excerpt: The generated KG in Neo4j demonstrates OntoKGen's ability to transform comprehensive technical documents into structured, actionable knowledge.
Every concept, sub-state, activity, and metric is correctly represented.
conducting this quantitative analysis and presenting those results are beyond the scope and limitations of this paper.
